hints: Focus on comparing the same mass of nitrogen in two different molar masses, so start by working out the $M_r$ of each salt.
Both salts contain 2 N atoms per formula unit, so the lighter $M_r$ will give the higher % N, calculate $28/M_r \times 100$ for each.
Consider what the ammonium ion, $\text{NH}_4^+$, does in water as the conjugate acid of a weak base, and what that means for $\text{H}^+$ concentration and pH.
walkthrough:
**Find the percentage of nitrogen by mass**

Both salts contain two nitrogen atoms per formula unit, so mass of N = $2 \times 14 = 28$.

Calculate $M_r$ for each salt:
$$M_r((\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4) = 28 + 8 + 32 + 64 = 132$$
$$M_r(\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3) = 14 + 4 + 14 + 48 = 80$$

**Compare the percentages**

Use % N = $28 / M_r \times 100$.

For sulfate: $28/132 \times 100 = 21.2\%$. For nitrate: $28/80 \times 100 = 35.0\%$.

So ammonium nitrate has the higher percentage of nitrogen by mass because it has the much smaller $M_r$.

**Decide the effect on soil pH**

Both salts contain the $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion, which is the conjugate acid of the weak base ammonia.

In wet soil it hydrolyses and releases $\text{H}^+$:
$$\text{NH}_4^+(\text{aq}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_3(\text{aq}) + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+(\text{aq})$$
This increase in $\text{H}^+$ concentration lowers pH, so both salts decrease the pH of neutral soil.

options.A: Correct. Ammonium nitrate ($M_r = 80$) has about 35% N compared to about 21% N for ammonium sulfate ($M_r = 132$), and the acidic $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion hydrolyses in water to produce $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$, decreasing soil pH.
options.B: Half right but wrong on pH. Ammonium nitrate does have the higher % N, but $\text{NH}_4^+$ is acidic, not basic. Students who think ammonium salts are alkaline or that nitrate ion raises pH may wrongly choose increase.
options.C: Half right but wrong on % N. Both salts do decrease pH, but ammonium sulfate has the lower % N because its $M_r$ of 132 is much larger. Students who only look at the sulfate being heavier without calculating often guess incorrectly.
options.D: Wrong on both parts. Ammonium sulfate has the lower % N, and it decreases pH rather than increasing it. Choosing increase suggests confusing the $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion with free ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, which is basic.
